conventions.name: 5TC basket, 180,000 t (to 24 December 2025)
conventions.rule: C5TC = Sum(C8_14 x 0.25, C9_14 x 0.125, C10_14 x 0.25, C14 x 0.25, C16 x 0.125), the Baltic Capesize (BCI180) of 180,000 dwt, every route at 5 percent total commission
conventions.source: Baltic Exchange, Guide to Market Benchmarks v7.09 (December 2025)

conventions.name: 5TC basket, 182,000 t (from 2 January 2026)
conventions.source: Baltic Exchange, Guide to Market Benchmarks v8.8 (September 2026)

conventions.name: Capesize futures, EEX
conventions.rule: CPTM (180,000 t basket) and C5TM (182,000 t basket): one day a lot, USD a day to two decimals, the underlying the arithmetic average of all the Baltic's daily assessments of the month; December's last registration day is 24 December. (BDRY's filings name its 180 kt contract C5TCM, a data vendor ticker.)
conventions.source: EEX Contract Specifications for Trade Registration, release 047a (23 July 2026)

conventions.name: TD3C route
conventions.rule: 270,000 t Middle East Gulf to China (Ras Tanura to Ningbo), laydays 15/30 days from index date, age max 15 years, 3.75 percent total commission; published in Worldscale (TD3C), in USD a tonne (TD3C$) and as a round-trip TCE (TD3C-TCE: 2 days load, 2 discharge, 2 waiting)
conventions.source: Baltic Exchange, Guide to Market Benchmarks v8.8 (September 2026)

conventions.name: TD3C futures, ICE (TDL)
conventions.rule: 1,000 t a lot, USD a tonne to 0.0001; final settlement the average of the Baltic's assessments for each Baltic publication day of the month; December expires on the 24th or the business day before
conventions.source: ICE Futures Europe, TD3C FFA Middle East Gulf to China (Baltic) Future (TDL), contract specification

conventions.name: Gross against net
conventions.rule: A time charter index and its FFA are gross daily hire; a voyage TCE is net of commission and is grossed up by it before the comparison; the owner keeps the net share, so its hedge is the voyage's days times that share
conventions.source: Baltic Exchange, Guide to Market Benchmarks v8.8 (September 2026)

conventions.name: Baltic standard Capesize of the date
conventions.rule: BCI182 from 2 January 2026: 14 knots on 52 t laden, 44 t ballast (GMB v8.8 page 78). BCI180 before: 14 knots laden or 15 knots ballast on 62 t, 12 or 13 knots on 43 t (GMB v7.09 page 76). Each priced at its fastest pairs.
conventions.source: Baltic Exchange, Guide to Market Benchmarks v8.8 (September 2026); Baltic Exchange, Guide to Market Benchmarks v7.09 (December 2025)

conventions.name: Publication days
conventions.rule: London business days: weekdays less England and Wales bank holidays, by statute and proclamation
conventions.source: Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971; Amplify Commodity Trust 10-Q (30 September 2025)

coverage.published_months: May to June 2023; August 2023 to December 2025

formulas.name: Settlement
formulas.text: S(month) = average of the Baltic's assessments on every publication day of the month; a quarter is the average of its three months

formulas.name: Basis
formulas.text: basis = FFA - spot, per tenor, on the same basket

formulas.name: Strip
formulas.text: F0 = sum over months of days(month) x F(month) / voyage days, days counted from the fixture date

formulas.name: Hedge size
formulas.text: FFA days in a month = voyage days in that month x (1 - commission) x k; TD3C in tonnes equal to the cargo

formulas.name: Paper
formulas.text: short (owner): (F0 - S) x size; long (charterer): (S - F0) x size

formulas.name: Surprise
formulas.text: U = gross TCE - F0; hedged = U - k (S - F0); effectiveness = 1 - Var(hedged) / Var(U)

formulas.name: Residual at k = 1
formulas.text: TCE - S = (TCE - 5TC on the day) route + (5TC on the day - S on the ship's basket) timing + (S ship - S curve) size

formulas.name: Forecast error
formulas.text: error = S - F(h months before expiry); roll cost of a rolling long = F - S (positive: the long pays, the short earns)

formulas.name: Worldscale
formulas.text: USD a tonne = WS / 100 x flat rate

limitations.text: There is no signal, no position sizing and no profit and loss presented as a strategy. Forward bias and roll cost are costs and premiums a hedger faces, reported as such.
limitations.title: A hedging study, not a forecast or a strategy

limitations.text: A month's settlement is the study's own average only when every London publication day is in a public print or implied by the next day's printed change (July 2023; January to October 2026); otherwise it is the average Himalaya Shipping published in its SEC filings (May 2023 onwards), which agrees with every complete month to within a dollar. Earlier months have only partial averages and enter the robustness checks alone.
limitations.title: The daily 5TC is public in full only from January 2026

limitations.text: Banchero Costa's weekly (mostly Monday) Capesize FFA assessments as Hellenic Shipping News republishes them, 8 January 2021 to 15 November 2026, with gaps where issues were not reachable. The next issue's previous-week column is a re-assessment; the study uses first prints and shows the latest as a sensitivity.
limitations.title: The forward curve is one broker's weekly assessment

limitations.text: 135 of 332 issues had at least one table set in fonts that do not extract as text. A row read by OCR is kept only if it reproduces its own printed week-on-week change (bunkers: the printed spread between grades).
limitations.title: Some tables were read by OCR

limitations.text: C3 and C5 TCEs come from the voyage engine with the Baltic's standard ship of the date and that week's Singapore bunkers. Port charges and loading time at the port's scale have no public figure and are left out, so the level of the route basis is overstated; its variability, which drives the results, is not. No route FFA is used: a voyage hedged with 5TC paper carries route basis by construction.
limitations.title: Voyage earnings are estimates, not fixtures

limitations.text: Hedged fixtures with exact settlements start on 5 May 2023; the out-of-sample hedge ratio needs 52 settled fixtures first, so it covers the later part of the sample only. Intervals are wide and a percentile interval can sit off its estimate in small samples.
limitations.title: The hedge sample is short

limitations.text: The Baltic's weekly reports give TD3C in Worldscale. Flat rates are licensed and never stated; dated public pairs (a Breakwave dollar print and the Baltic's Worldscale print four days earlier) imply a consistent one only in the second half of 2025, so the study keeps Worldscale and the dollar case studies use Breakwave's bi-weekly prints, a month settled at the average of its one to three prints. A month with one print settles at its own fixture, so the share of variance a TD3C hedge removes is not computed (too few months have two prints); the forward errors are, labelled approximate.
limitations.title: TD3C in dollars a tonne is approximate

limitations.text: Their publishers' and repositories' sites could not be reached when the data were gathered, so no published result is quoted; Ederington's measure is reported for the reader to set beside them.
limitations.title: The published hedging studies could not be obtained

policy.decision: Daily values stay in the ignored cache. Committed: monthly settlement averages, derived statistics, and weekly TD3C and TD34 prints each with the link it was read from.
policy.source: Baltic Exchange indices (5TC daily, TD3C, TD34)

policy.decision: The extracted panel stays in the ignored cache. Committed: derived statistics and the dated curves of the validation weeks and the latest week, each cited with its issue and page.
policy.source: Banchero Costa weekly report (FFA assessments, spot, routes, bunkers)

policy.decision: Public records: every quarter-end mark is committed with its filing's link.
Public records: the published monthly 5TC averages are committed with their links.
TD3C in USD a tonne and the futures index are committed as cited points with each report's link.
Daily prints stay in the cache; they enter only monthly averages and derived statistics.
Never published: only the test of whether dated pairs agree.

robustness.label: First prints, exact settlements (complete or published months), quarter proxies allowed
Latest print of each curve (the next issue's re-assessment) instead of the first
All months, estimated settlements of incomplete months included
Only months the study's own daily series completes (2026 and July 2023)
No quarter proxies: a voyage month must be printed as a month
robustness.note: the forecast errors equal the headline's; no fixture qualifies for 5TC trip at 3 months, C3 at 2 months, C3 at 3 months, C5 at 3 months

robustness.note: a 2026 price and its settlement move by the same fixed USD 3,503, so forecast errors cannot change
